name: @osionos/graph-engine
description: Self-contained force-graph engine (Canvas2D + Web Worker d3-force) with an aurora-glass visual language and a thin React adapter. Decoupled from any host app: feed it a GraphModel, it renders. Theme resolves --osio-* CSS custom properties at runtime — see README's Limitations section for what that means standalone.
//engines: Node >=22.6 is REQUIRED, not advisory: the test script uses --experimental-strip-types, and `node --test` on Node 20 dies with `node: bad option: --experimental-strip-types`. Matches the host repo, which pins 22.x. Run the gate in Docker (see Dockerfile) so you never depend on the host's Node.
//devDependencies: Peers are duplicated here on purpose: npm install does not install peer deps, so without these the standalone typecheck cannot resolve them and the check fails on a package that is actually fine. Versions are the ones osionos's own pnpm-lock.yaml resolved, not guessed — and the eslint toolchain is PINNED EXACT rather than caret-ranged, because a range silently pulled eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1, whose new `react-hooks/refs` rule fails on src/react/useGraphEngine.ts:35 under a rule the host's locked 7.0.1 does not have. Same class of drift as a stale lockfile; pin it. vite is deliberately ABSENT: the package ships no build and no dev server, and a bundler is the consumer's choice.

scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
